thesis: A refiner is long the crack spread, not long crude, so the US-Iran supply disruption that put Brent at 94.09 on 08-21 is a margin expansion rather than a cost problem - which is why DINO rose 4.96% on Friday to 97.32 while integrated energy (XLE) fell 0.17%. A US-Iran ceasefire headline collapses the crude premium and the crack spread together, and with a 3.76% ATR the 86.5 stop is only 2.9 ATR away - one gap-down weekend headline can jump it.
counter_argument: Crack spreads are mean-reverting and the strongest version of this trade was in May at 69, not at 97 after a 107% run. The insider buys are two people at one company, and Myers own 08-11 purchase at 85.30 is already 14% underwater in reverse - i.e. he would not pay today s price either.

thesis: A war that disrupts Gulf supply does not destroy refined-product demand, it lengthens the voyage that satisfies it - product tankers get paid on ton-miles, so rerouting around a disrupted Middle East is a rate increase rather than a volume loss. STNG is the laggard expression of a move the peers have already made: it sits 10.18% below its 120-day high of 87.39 while FRO is only 3.32% below its own and INSW 2.77%, and it has coiled between its 20-day (77.53) and 50-day (77.16) all week while Brent settled 94.09.
key_risk: The peer gap may be information rather than opportunity - STNG carries product-tanker exposure while FRO and INSW are weighted to crude, and if the disruption is crude-specific the laggard simply stays a laggard. Sizing is speculative at 2% for that reason. Note also that the insider data returned for STNG this morning was corrupt (a $5.87 purchase price on a $78 stock and $18.9B of reported sales), so no insider signal is claimed here in either direction.
counter_argument: Tanker equities are late-cycle by the time the war is on the front page; the spot rate spike is already in FRO and INSW, and STNG lagging through a week when the driver was at its most intense is the market telling you which vessel class is actually getting paid.

thesis: This is a re-pitch at an unchanged level, not a new idea - published 2026-08-21 at 398.00 and never filled. Buying the recovery assumes the drawdown was the aberration rather than the correction.

catalyst.event: FDA PDUFA target action date for the deramiocel BLA (Duchenne muscular dystrophy cardiomyopathy), Class 2 resubmission
catalyst.action: WAIT - the decision resolves TODAY, before the next open, so there is no pre-event entry available. Act only on the outcome, and only on the rejection branch.

thesis: The tension worth owning is that the FDA panel and the phase 3 were answering different questions: the July advisory committee voted 3-9 against evidence of effectiveness in DMD *cardiomyopathy*, while HOPE-3 - published in The Lancet and the reason the stock went 4.21 to 6.65 on 66.3M shares on 08-14 - met its primary endpoint on *upper limb* progression (PUL 2.0, p=0.029) with nominally significant cardiac measures alongside. A complete response letter on the cardiomyopathy indication therefore does not delete the Lancet dataset or the upper-limb path, but a washout to the pre-Lancet 4.21 price would be priced as though it had.
key_risk: This is a conviction-2 lottery ticket and its evidence is one-sided and thin - it rests on a single reading of one advisory committee vote, and is sized at 1% accordingly. The concrete dangers are specific: Capricor posted a ~$40.7M Q2 loss, so a CRL is followed by a dilutive raise with near-certainty, and a secondary is the most likely way this thesis dies before the regulatory question is settled. ATR14 is 14.34% on a $6.29 stock, halts around an FDA decision are routine, and a second CRL could reasonably end the company rather than merely dent it.
counter_argument: The FDA follows its advisory committees most of the time, and a 3-9 vote is not a close call - the base case is rejection, which is exactly why the stock has already faded 21% from 7.98 on 08-19 to 6.29. Buying the washout assumes the market will overshoot on news it has spent a week pre-positioning for, and the 120-day high of 36.82 is a reminder that this equity has already destroyed 83% of its value on precisely this storyline.

catalyst.action: accumulate in thirds across 104-122 over the next two quarters; the 09-02 print is an opportunity to buy the last third, not a reason to wait for the whole position

thesis: A brand this strong does not de-rate 41% from 205.07 to 121.07 on a demand problem - it de-rated on a merchandising problem the interim CEO named out loud, product launches that failed to wow shoppers, and a 410bp Q1 gross-margin contraction from tariffs and discounting. Those are fixable by a person, and the company hired a specific one: Heidi ONeill, who ran Consumer, Product and Brand at Nike for part of 28 years there, starts 09-08. The insiders are already acting on it - board chair Charles Bergh bought 6,090 shares at 164.20 on 03-20 and then 4,275 more at 117.05 on 06-15, averaging down with his own money, with Andre Maestrini buying 3,275 at 151.02 between them: 3 open-market buys, 2 distinct buyers, $1.99M bought against $100K sold.
key_risk: The invalidation is concrete and not a price move: if North American comparable sales are still negative two quarters after ONeill takes over, or gross margin fails to recover at least half of the 410bp it lost for two consecutive quarters, the problem is the brand rather than the merchandising and this thesis is wrong. FY2026 guidance is already cut to $11.0-11.15B revenue - flat to down 1% - with EPS of $10.95-11.15 against a $12.29 estimate, so the company is not yet growing.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that a lower valuation does not fix the problems: US revenue and comps fell materially year on year while the growth is in China, which is a harder, lower-margin market to win, and tariffs are a cost the new CEO cannot merchandise away. Bergh is also the board chair who presided over the de-rating, so his buying is not a disinterested outside signal.

instrument: Fed rate decision in September 2026 - Hike 25bps (YES)

entry.condition: 32 is the live ask (bid 31 / ask 32). Do not pay above 34 - the whole idea is the size of the gap to my estimate, so overpaying deletes the edge.

exit.scale_plan: the August CPI print on ~09-11 resolves before the 09-16 FOMC and is the natural repricing event - trim half there if it prints above 3.4%, hold the rest to resolution

catalyst.event: FOMC decision, resolving the Sep 2026 Fed rate decision market. August CPI prints ~09-11, before resolution, and is the intermediate repricing event.
catalyst.action: buy the YES at 32c now; this is exitable before resolution rather than a forced hold, because the 09-11 CPI print moves it

thesis: The market prices Hike 25bps at 31c against Fed maintains at 68c and a 25bp cut at 1c, on 2.76M contracts of volume - and the same exchange prices August CPI YoY at 3.3% central (Above 3.2% = 87c, Above 3.3% = 69c). My estimate is roughly 42%, not 31%. The gap exists because the market is anchored to the correct default that the Fed holds, and that default was set before Brent broke 94.09 on a live US-Iran supply disruption whose pass-through lands in the August and September prints. Three things compound it: a chair who is new and whose public record is consistently hawkish, a first Jackson Hole keynote on 08-28 which is exactly where a chair buys credibility, and 4.1% unemployment with a 5c recession probability giving him the room to use it.
key_risk: Conviction 2 and its evidence is thin and one-sided - this is one reading of one policy setup, sized at 1% as a lottery ticket, and the honest description is a directional lean rather than a modelled probability. The specific way it is wrong: central banks conventionally look THROUGH an energy supply shock rather than tightening into it, because a war premium is not demand-driven inflation. Robinhood also charges a probability-weighted commission capped at 1c per contract, which is material against a 32c entry.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is political and it is strong: Treasury Secretary Bessent has been publicly pressuring this Fed to ease, and a brand-new chair facing that pressure is more likely to hold than to hike in his first months. Robinhoods own Number of rate cuts in 2026 market prices exactly 0 cuts at 86% - which confirms no cut is coming but says nothing about a hike, and a hold at 68c may simply be correct.
